q: Calculate the temperature change for each reaction.
Classify each reaction as exothermic or endothermic.
A and C are exothermic (warmer). B and D are endothermic (colder).
Explain what happens to energy in reaction D.
Energy is taken in from the surroundings (the water and cup) and stored in the products, so the surroundings get colder.
A student says C releases twice the energy of A. Evaluate this.
Only true if the amounts and volumes were the same; the temperature rise depends on how much reacted and the mass of liquid heated. The table does not say, so we cannot be sure.
